# NOTES

## BOOK 1 of 2: *English Ways and By-Ways* (Parks, 1920)

**Form/cast:** Letters from John & Ruth Dobson (US Episcopal parson, Ulster/Welsh ancestry; Ruth of Boston, English stock, sister in Yorkshire) to friend Leighton Parks, who is temporarily blind (Miss Fuller reads letters to him). Also: Rex (Irish setter, Mr. Dennis's gift, dies Good Friday). Dedication: E.S.P. Preface: humorous, "sympathetic banter" aims to ease tension before WWI. Pre-war England, 1914 era. Thanks to *Atlantic Monthly*.

**Ch I The Legacy:** Good Friday, John calls "Hello, Rex!", dog leaps from study window, dies on steps. John: "I wish it were I." Ruth gives him tea, pipe. Carpenter Mr. Hathaway makes box. Burial at Mabel Wheelock's place, Pelham; taxi $7; Ruth's new Easter hat, store woman waives cost. Dr. Webster: "You can't afford to keep on." Gushy parishioner: "salt in lumps." Easter: lawyers Weeks & Burke; Aunt Susan B. Melchor (California) dies, leaves money. Tradition: she was shocked at John's father's engagement; tried to win father; later fond of John as boy. John: "Lakewood be blowed!" Going to Europe. "lay down for a sunny day."

**Ch II School of Instruction:** Motor trip plan (Ruth's economy). Driving school run by "Professor" Patrick Quinn, NYC, Jerome Avenue. Profanity; "damn awkward." Near-accident on Concourse bridge; Quinn's prayer "O my G--d... Vanderbilt Cup race." Quinn's Fabian passing tactics; calls rivals "brother." Narrator quits school without diploma.

**Ch III "Fool Proof":** Cheap two-cylinder car rejected (salesman: silent cars dangerous; Ruth: "no conversation possible"). Buys Frontenac runabout (new "gentleman's" model, folding seat, self-starter); salesman: "practically 'FOOL PROOF.'" Drives in park three times before shipping.

**Ch IV "Der Kaiser Wilhelm der Zweite":** Crossing. Poker invitation, "twenty-five cents a point"; "De trouble mit men who hafe lifed all der lives in a village." Sunday service in Lounge; band plays "Ein Feste Burg"; Jewish guest: "If Christians began by treating us as if we were human..." John prays for Kaiser first time. Plymouth arrival; mine-explosions salutes ("childish way"); officer: "they will some day learn."

**Ch V The Car Arrives:** Ruth goes ahead by train to sister in Yorkshire. Car on *Georgic* at Tilbury (25 miles from London). Third officer on docks/vacuum cleaners idea; "Are these things necessities? Then let us meet them like necessities." Casual laborer: "You 'ave fergot the 'andle, sir!" Chauffeur: American cars not durable; "There are changes; I do not know that they are always improvements." Garage near Leicester Square.

**Ch VI The Great North Road:** Leaves London westward via Regent Park; first night Hatfield, "Purple Cow" inn near GNR tracks. Ostler, "Ichabod," old coaching days. Lost road—20+ miles too far east near Cambridge; laborer's superiority; reaches Royston. Hatfield House, Salisbury/Gladstone musings. Literary associations: Jeanie Deans, Squeers, Pickwick.

**Ch VII The England of Fielding:** Inn "Dappled Hart" (lamb, peas, cherry tart). Bar: drummer, village doctor, landlord; discussion of public "Convenience"; doctor "a medical man myself"; Squire Westons, Dogberry, landlord's "midden."

**Ch VIII End of the North Road:** Near-collision with touring car on wrong (left) side; Henry and wife in tonneau: "it is an American, and he is on the wrong side of the road!" Narrator's "bête." Wife's rage ("claws"). Learns: right side wrong side in England; 20 mph/"thirty" to average 20. Peterborough inn archway wrecks mudguard. Cathedral: Durham, Lincoln, Ely, Gloucester comparisons. Trent/Newark; Hotspur's "monstrous cantle." Fountains Abbey; arrives at the "Beeches."

**Ch IX An English Interior:** Writes "inside" letter at the Beeches. John tinkers with car; William the boy ("Spanner, sir, yes, sir"); Sir Thomas; Maud (Ruth's sister, wife of Sir Thomas); Thomas's chauffeur. Servants: "pancake minder side," specialization; "give warning"; Mary Maloney/Mrs. McCarthy Boston servants; Under-housemaid's "correct insolence." Captain Hyde of Silver Harbor.

**Ch X Husband and Wife:** Nanny Miles (nurse); Ruth on trained nurses; Edward "my business is rather urgent." Maud: Nanny as feudal survival; "Can you imagine Miles taking a place with the Rosenthals?" Fathers/husbands run households; "Englishwomen... companionship of their husbands." Dinner rules: butler "Dinner is served, Sir Thomas!"; Sir Thomas's explanations: aisle seat/flintlocks; host notified for leading lady. Ruth: "English can give a reason."

**Ch XI The Fourth Speed:** Brother-in-law: "jolly good thing... if tired of... my wife." Descent near Sawley (near Ripon); foot brake fine; narrator pulls fourth-speed lever not emergency brake. Picnic pony-cart; boy "Oh, I say!" Laborer: "there be two of 'em." Young couple tip: switch off current, use clutch/engine as brake; "highest passes of the Alps... without touching the brake."

**Ch XII "Jael the Wife of Heber the Kenite":** Sunday; Ruth writes. John's "Lying can be the highest form of truth." Cathedral sermon: Jael as type of Blessed Virgin; John walks out. Diatribe on Established Church ("stench"). "Sands o' Dee" recited (Kingsley). Evensong sermon on "I know where thou dwellest"; anthem "Love Divine."

**Ch XIII "As It Was in the Beginning":** Garden stranger questions: John's Jael remark; "Really, I should never have suspected [you're American]"; Ruth: John's ancestry Ulster/Wales, hers Norfolk/Devon. Stranger (son-in-law chapel, Lloyd George/Asquith), argues church as "bulwark of society"; "As it was in the beginning, is now and ever shall be." Narrator's comforting reflection; "not been a restful day."

**Ch XIV Rural England:** Road from "Barchester" to Gloucester. Huntsman "James the Huntsman, The Kennels, Blankshire" (Ruth's kodak); "Ivanhoe"; Gurth/Robin Hood; "You talk like William Jennings Bryan." Horseman's brother of Derby winner; shepherd & dog. Houses (Queen Anne, Elizabethan). Ruth: servility/kowtowing; "you are exactly like Crugan." Tom Crugan story: Hoboken; "Why the hell can't you keep your belly out of my brake?"

**Ch XV Education:** Gloucester (Saxon/Norman layers; "Chambered Nautilus"); Wells west front. Bath hotel (Brummel). Winchester; St. Cross pilgrims (bread and ale); house master. English standards: Latin prose; boys to prep at 8–9. Narrator's reasons (climate, nervous American boys, father decides on boarding). Prof. Corson: "Any except 'Education'!"

**Ch XVI A By-Election:** Salisbury cathedral ("built, not grown"); Ruth: Martin Chuzzlewit. Gentleman advises route across Plain; Stonehenge. Village Divises, by-election, Labor (Bowles) on saloon regulation vs Conservative "free rum." Parson drives little girl on pony with blue ribbons, toasts "The King and the Church." Young man's mother's sitting room; Ruth given tea. "Vested interests... so radical."

**Ch XVII Sheep-Dogs:** Wye valley from Ross; Tintern Abbey; Wordsworth poem. Cart shaft punctures radiator (farmer: "like 'avin' your horse took with the gripes"). Cyclist plugs radiator. Garage wrong-kind radiator. Sheep-dog trial on farm; dog gathers flock into pens, bell-wether, "Was it well done?"

**Ch XVIII Brigands and Bootblacks:** Train trip to visit parents of parish lad; Captain Burchell (retired naval, silent); Mrs. Burchell fears America, brigands, "dissenters from the church of Christ," Fifteenth Avenue Church; Bessie Salter's boot-blacking "grinning 'nigger.'" Ruth laughs; "dear old things think of us as... colony."

**Ch XIX The Piston-Rod:** Ride through Shropshire/Kent; Ruth on emigrant Englishmen. Broken glass/tires guarantee. Noise: valves Nos. 2 and 4; "broken piston-rod" diagnosis; urchin: "Your tire's flat!" Nail in rear tire; rim change "three minutes... and twenty-seven more." Narrator's sarcasm; "It's all right, honey."

**Ch XX Falstaff:** Shrewsbury: front wheels slip onto sidewalk, tea hour, tree/wall; garage of the "Raven." Battlefield of Shrewsbury; Shakespeare as Pied Piper; Falstaff/Hotspur moral musings. Mr. Rhodes (historian) "new lie of Falstaff's... Shrewsbury clock." Plans change: letters; leave motor.

**Ch XXI The Black Country:** Archdeacon Williams (invites; no smoke; faith quality vs quantity; mathematician). Daily schedule: prayers, study, dinner, Mrs. Williams "asphyxiated by dull wives." Children: Rose (~12), Dick, Edward. Sunday-school treat, van; man at tea, "first time... talked with a gentleman"; cotton famine, John Bright. Rose and "fly" (horse cab) 10 shillings, "Not living!", "bug and fly." "Dick said Americans bounders."

**Ch XXII An "Average" Sunday:** Archdeacon's mission sermon; parable of Sower ("soil is human nature"); education argument; Jews/Catholics; "Securalists." Narrator's sermon weak (Ruth's whisper: "Better be dull and decent"). Station: guard gives first-class seat.

**Ch XXIII Dowager and Cowboy:** John visits Archdeacon Williams. Narrator to Shelburnes (Gertrude; Admiral Sir George Shelburne, "Lady's walk"); guest secretary with despatch-box; Guy (naval officer). Lady Agatha Bumstead's Tweed/Erie anecdote; Cheyenne cowboy "He spat!" "Always a pleasure to help a lady!"

**Ch XXIV "By Pureness...":** Ruth's wire; Stratford skipped; Banbury, Oxford, Ipswich (Pickwick inn). Sanfords (Sharrow; non-juror bed; strong Ceylon tea). Sunday: Mr. Sanford's Bible reading; parson distrains Scroston's cow. "Look round" hike; farmer, "white ones is 'saft'"; supper prayers; Sanford's apology to servants. Ruth: "become a Tory?"

**Ch XXV The County Families:** Maypole inn (Barnaby Rudge). Drive through East End London to Garvin's Private Hotel (telegram in porters' rack; "Lexington Avenue boarding-house"). Old squire's hat talk; bathrooms story (Chicago bellboy maid). John's roses "sin-offering."

**Ch XXVI The Boat-Race:** Ingrams from Boston; Mortlake; Harvard lost to Cambridge; lad "Which won?" Man rebukes narrator. Siegels at Maidenhead: "Chilled Steel"; Harvard training "bromide."

**Ch XXVII The Custom-House:** Jim Siegel, grandfather 1848 Schurz; Frankfort trunks (Maria, Charlie Wilson); porter's field-marshal uniform; locksmith; Munich locks. Ruth dislikes his exaggeration.

**Ch XXVIII The "Rob" Room:** Windsor (White Heifer). Athanasian Creed; "Rob" room joke; Buckthorne dinner (Miss Buckthorne, precedence/"experimenting" butler).

**Ch XXIX Vested Interests:** Sir William (Reading area), rector's abuses; bishop's "vested interest." Mr. Buckthorne: parson shot partridges "sitting."

**Ch XXX "The Auld Un'":** Knickerbockers; ferrets; narrator shoots favorite ferret; Jenkins; pheasant out of season. Jock.

**Ch XXXI Church and State:** Malvern; Abbey sermon; Dreyfus-like "Cause Célèbre" verdict; vicar's notices on prayer; smoking room; ladies on lynching, John Burns.

**Ch XXXII The Chaplain to the Queen:** Betts-y-Coed, Waterloo hotel; John the porter's voice; Celtic vs Saxon. Rev. Henry Waitland; Queen's chaplain; Ponsonby's collect.

**Ch XXXIII The Retired Colonel:** Llandudno sands; children; Ruth's blue-eyed angel; Philistines; war fears; Colonel "My G--d!" Dr. Weir Mitchell mosquito anecdote.

**Ch XXXIV A Problem in Casuistry:** Cork; Killarney; "it ain't properly got two sides"; giant at hovel and Blarney Castle wrong road; Lord Chesterfield coal-mine joke.

**Ch XXXV A Day of Trouble and Distress:** Self-starter fails; cul-de-sac; Ruth grabs dog's tail; narrator swears; level crossing, Dublin express; Ross, Ruth weeps. Dublin: Hodges (professor, Packard, Anne); batteries; Dublin Castle. Holyhead; Waterloo.

**Ch XXXVI "One Every Minute":** Barchester hotel; Frontenac battery trouble; Maud's telegram; Ruth stays; Banbury; Frontenac manager; music-hall (Chevallier, Sarah Bernhardt); "headlights left on for three weeks." Manager: "One Every Minute."

**Ch XXXVII Anglia or Frontenac?:** Ruth's doctor (Maud's pet): pregnant; return on *Adriatic*. Narrator's apologia; baby named "John" (Ruth's choice). Car on dock at Tilbury.

## BOOK 2 of 2: *Girl Scouts in Arizona and New Mexico* (Roy, 1923)

**Cast:** Julie (Juliet) Lee, leader, writer for *Elmertown Record* (secret; wants to be author); Betty Lee (twin, timid, "Gilly, do you mind?"); Mrs. Vernon ("Verny," Captain, Dandelion Troop founder); Mr. Vernon ("Unk Verny"); Mr. Gilroy ("Gilly," "Gilly-of-the-Dandelioners," Denver, Adirondack estate, Boss); Joan Allison (corporal, chum of Julie); Hester Wynant ("Hesty"); Anne Bailey (big eater; sister Eleanor's wedding); Amy Ward; Judith (Judy) & Edith Blake; Ruth Bentley (to Europe); Mary (maid); Tally (Indian guide, Boss = Gilroy, "Mees Jule," "Mebbe"); Omney (English party); Tom Sanderson ("Sandy," Forest Ranger, Panchuelo, Univ. Albuquerque); Mr. Burt (newspaper correspondent, Denver/Pueblo Indian article); Adair, Chase (college men; Adair = dark, Chase = blond); Padre Miguel (88, Santa Fé); Ranger Johnson, Ranger Oliver (Grass Mountain); Mr. Balmore (Laguna); Mr. Walters (Gallup hotel manager); Lo/Lorenzo (Navajo guide); Lorenzo Hubbell ("King"); Bill & Ben (horse thieves).

**Ch 1 Plans for the Southwest Trip:** Elmertown, first day of summer vacation, Mrs. Vernon's home. Dandelion Troop origins (NJ Blue Mountains; Blue Beard's cave rescue of Mr. Gilroy; Adirondacks First Lake; Rockies with Gilroy). Patrols. Mothers Mrs. Blake (Grand Canyon fears), Mrs. Ward. Gilroy's letter (typed; "Gilly-of-the-Dandelioners"): desert items, flannel underwear, Chicago Limited from Philadelphia Sunday, Julie to flag train, suit-cases as pillows, route undecided; oculist in Loop. Anne: "Not living!" (no—"Not living" is Rose's, Book 2 Ch 5-ish). Mrs. Vernon: Gilroy's letter says Kansas City; Tally at La Junta; ice cream and layer-cake.

**Ch 2 Julie's Secret Ambition:** Chicago luncheon; Edgewater Beach; Lake Michigan colors; Pullman; Julie writes for *Elmertown Record* secretly. Kansas City (Mr. Vernon). La Junta: Tally ("Me pooly well"). Trinidad; Cardenas hotel. Packing list. Elk-skin boots from old Indian's family near Gray Mine road; moccasins; Mr. Vernon's $10 bill.

**Ch 3 On the Old Santa Fé Trail:** Horse-trader: nine ponies, three burros; insurance; ponies named White Star (Julie's), Slow Poke, Spark, Good-for-Nuttin' (Nuttin'), Sweetie (Joan's), Stick (Tally's mule). Raton Mountain; Forest Ranger Sanderson; camp; falls. Julie poses on hanging tree at cliff edge, falls; Tally climbs down, Gilroy and Vernon bring her up; ammonia (Mrs. Vernon's vial); Hester's camera wound to end of film. Note left on stick for Ranger.

**Ch 4 Julie Makes a Conquest:** Lake camp; Tally wrong trail; Sanderson night-rides, meets Tally ("Snubby" horse); Julie at breakfast; Sanderson smitten; Mr. Gilroy: "Julie's made a conquest"; Joan jealous; Old Trail history; River of Lost Souls.

**Ch 5 Sandy Has His Say:** Springer; Burt fails to appear; wire to Las Vegas Castañeda. Ride via Wagon Mound, Optimo, Valmora, Watrous. Reading room: Sanderson vs Burt on Bursum Bill, Mescalero bill, Pueblo water rights; Julie's secret letter to Burt; Joan watches.

**Ch 6 What Happened in the Pecos Forests:** Las Vegas; Hot Springs; Gallinas Canyon ice (60,000 tons). Pecos Forest (750,000 acres). Ranger Johnson; Apache Inn; Pecos Canyon; Grass Mountain. Tally's "Beaver and Porcupine" legend (Julie writes it down).

**Ch 7 Where Are the Burros?:** Oliver leads party to Lake Park; burros hobbled; next day Panchuelo; burros gone; tracks; tributary stream; Bishop's Lodge; Sanderson back from Santa Fé with men; Tally and Gilroy return at 11:45 p.m.

**Ch 8 Gilly Turns Forest Ranger:** Gilroy's account: Winsor smoke; fire fighting; "Ruins"; wind direction; Ranger Oliver; burros found.

**Ch 9 Tally and the Rustlers:** Tally, moccasins, horse-thieves Ben & Bill; rope bindings; fire-set by thieves; Tally rides back; Bishop's Lodge; reward $500 from New Yorkers; Tally refuses reward.

**Ch 10 Ancient Ruins and Modern Romance:** Bishop's Lodge; Sanderson with Adair, Chase; Tesuque, Cuyamunque, Nambe, Chimayo, Taos Pueblo (seven stories); Adair/Chase follow. San Juan, Santa Cruz, Puye Ruins; Santa Fé; Belnap's Ranch.

**Ch 11 Padre Miguel's Story:** Priest (88, 70 years in Santa Fé); Old Palace; Spanish lady tale; caravan; friar of Isleta (mummified body). Gilroy & Vernon plan automobiles.

**Ch 12 Julie's Tête-à-Tête:** Frijoles Canyon, cliff dwellings; Puye; Chaco Canyon trip. Friends from Denver arrive: Amy, Anne, Judith (surprise). Albuquerque (Alvarado Hotel); Sandy's "wish" at Enchanted Mesa; hotel dance; balcony; "Here's my post office address—Julie, dear!"

**Ch 13 The Enchanted Mesa:** Laguna (Balmore); wagons; mirage; Acoma (sky-city, 400 ft); Mrs. Vernon's plan: Arizona one month, Painted Desert, Petrified Forests, Grand Canyon, Hualapai, Prescott, Salt River, Gila, Apache Trail, Roosevelt Dam, Tucson, Galveston steamer.

**Ch 14 At St. Michael's Mission:** Conductor advice (Canyon de Chelly, White House); Gallup; El Navajo hotel; Walters; burros returned; trucks/cars; Navajo school; Superior; "White Feather" tent trick (John Sweetwater); Nature Game.

**Ch 15 The Painted Desert:** Julie's letters to Sanderson; Lo (Lorenzo) guide; Ganado; Lorenzo Hubbell; sandstorm; Joan's horse; Ream's (Keam's) Cañon; Kit Carson monument; Moki villages; Adamana; horses rest disputed.

**Ch 16 Region of Petrified Forests:** Gilroy's flood legend; First Forest (Eagle's Head, Petrified Bridge ~111 ft); Chalcedony Park; Rainbow Forest; Adamana inn; Flagstaff, Lowell Observatory; Julie's articles (Sunset Crater, Meteorite Mountain, Cañon Diablo); declines Montezuma's Castle; Tally sells pack-horses at Williams ($30 each; "$65 at St Michael's") — profit split.

**Ch 17 Bright Angel Trail:** Grand Canyon; Bass Camp; sunset; sunrise; Julie's mule on ledge; Indian Gardens; Jacob's Ladder; Devil's Corkscrew; Betty's fear; Hermit trail; Santa Maria Spring; Lion Cañon; birds, plants (ocatillo, Devil's Claw); Gilroy's telegram: Adirondack title dispute, court in September; party returns East; Tally "Don' leaf Tally outen dat mountain climb."

### Last words of text: Julie, "So _he_ says," laughed Julie, bound to have the last word.
